grammar.title: 4B: Ability and possibility - can, could, be able to
grammar.explanation:
Use **can** for things that are possible now. My aunt **can** cook very well.

Use **can't** when something is not possible now. A baby **can't** read a book.

Use **could** for things that were possible in the past. My uncle **could** run fast when he was a teenager.

Use **couldn't** when something was not possible in the past. Last year my niece **couldn't** swim.

Use **will be able to** for things that will be possible in the future. Next year my nephew **will be able to** read.

After **can** and **could**, use the verb alone. Say 'I **can** swim', never 'I **can to** swim'.
examples: My aunt *can* cook very well. (ability now)
A baby *can't* walk yet. (not possible now)
My uncle *could* play football when he was a teenager. (past ability)
My niece *couldn't* swim last year. (not possible in the past)
My nephew *will be able to* read books next year. (future ability)
I want *to be able to* drive a car. (be able to after another verb)
